The table below depicts the continued general gradual improvement in U.S. Industrial Equipment Spending
since December 2004. Capacity Utilization has remained above 80 percent since December 2005 while the PMI
has sustained a rate over 50 since December 2004. Although we have seen consistent strength over the past few
years in the manufacturing indicators we follow, we are seeing a deceleration in the rate of manufacturing growth
in the North American market.

ROK_2007_p35__paragraph_1.ocr:
In 2007, sales to non-U.S. customers accounted for 46 percent of our total sales. Outside the U.S., demand
for our products and services is principally driven by the strength of the industrial economy in each region and by
our customers’ ability and propensity to invest in their manufacturing assets. These customers may include both
multinational companies with expanding global presence and a growing number of local companies. Recent
strength in demand for our products and services has, in part, been driven by investments in infrastructure in
developing economies, investments in basic materials production capacity in response to higher commodity
pricing and expanding consumer markets. We continued to see strong demand in China, India and Latin America
during 2007. We also saw considerable growth in Europe during 2007, as we benefited from our targeted growth
investments in customer-facing resources and improving macro-economic conditions. We expect strong growth
in Latin America, Europe and the emerging economies in Asia-Pacific to continue into 2008.
